_readme: AN ASTEROID INTO THE ATLANTIC, SEEN FROM ABOVE (2026-10-25; docs/WATER_V2.md section 13). A 10 km
impactor at 20 km/s lands at 35 N 42 W, the middle of the North Atlantic, at the scene's start. Its
cavity (laws/Impact.hlsli: Ward & Asphaug's lipped parabola, ~110 km across, as deep as the ocean)
evolves by linear dispersive theory, and the globe's vertices sum that law: the ring of the first wave
crosses the basin at sqrt(g h) ~ 200 m/s. The clock runs 240x so the four hours to the American
shelf pass in a minute. The drawn wave is exaggerated 10x (exag, on the deep wave before the
shoaling's bound); the physics is raw.
`impacts` is the RECORD of events (sim/ImpactField.h); press I over the sea to drop another
(`sea.impactor`) at the point under the cursor, at the clock's instant.
The companion scene impact_newburyport.json stands on the beach for the same event's arrival.
